title: FUSE-TCAD: A Diffusion-Based Multi-Field Surrogate for High-Fidelity TCAD Device Simulation
evidence_span: FUSE-TCAD uses a diffusion-based conditional surrogate to generate joint physical fields under continuous geometry and bias control, with physics-aware Sobolev-edge regularization. On SOI-FET datasets it uses 20% target-domain data for transfer learning, reports more than 30x speedup over commercial TCAD, and maintains relative error within 0.8%.
problem: Traditional TCAD solves coupled PDEs at high cost, while scalar ML surrogates discard field-level physical information needed for device analysis and optimization.
method_or_artifact: Conditional diffusion surrogate for joint physical-field distributions, with geometry/bias injection, physics-aware Sobolev-edge regularization, and target-domain transfer learning.
workload_or_benchmark: SOI-FET device datasets across geometry and bias conditions; field prediction and transfer-learning evaluation.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: TCAD device simulation and SOI-FET process conditions; commercial TCAD comparison, solver configuration, field resolution, and target-domain shift are not exposed in the description.
metrics: cross-field consistency and high-fidelity field prediction
limits: The description does not provide field-by-field error distributions, PDE residual definitions, resolution, solver hardware, transfer baselines, or commercial-tool measurement conditions; the speedup and error claims require paper-level verification.

title: Fusedot: A Multiplication-Fused Dot Product Accelerator for Efficient LLM Inference
evidence_span: FuseDot exploits identical-weight multiplication opportunities in low-bit mixed-precision LLM inference through a multiplication-fused dot-product paradigm. It combines index-driven generalized matrix multiplication, hierarchical dual-phase reordering, and cross-PE multiplier sharing with a half-multiplier scheme, reporting 1.51–1.98x speedup and 1.19–1.51x energy-efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art accelerators.
problem: Mixed-precision FP16xINT4 LLM inference remains multiplication-heavy on general-purpose processors and conventional dot-product accelerators.
method_or_artifact: MFDP multiplication-fused dot-product paradigm with index-driven generalized matrix multiplication, hierarchical dual-phase reordering, and cross-processing-element multiplier sharing.
workload_or_benchmark: Low-bit mixed-precision LLM inference; exact model suite, sequence lengths, and accelerator configurations are not stated in the description.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Specialized accelerator with multiple processing elements and half-multiplier sharing; quantization formats and memory/interconnect assumptions beyond FP16xINT4 are unspecified.
baselines: general-purpose processors (motivation, not measured in the description)
limits: The description omits models, sequence lengths, accuracy impact, area, frequency, memory traffic, and exact baseline hardware; reported ranges require paper-level conditions and variance.

title: Xsearch: Exploring Microarchitecture Design Space Through Bayesian Optimization and Cross Evaluation on Multi-Fidelity Simulators
evidence_span: XSearch addresses the efficiency–accuracy trade-off in microarchitecture design-space exploration by using multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization. It explores more points with low-fidelity simulation and calibrates or cross-evaluates candidates with high-fidelity simulation; the method is applied to the open-source XiangShan high-performance processor core.
problem: Microarchitecture design-space exploration must balance expensive accurate simulation against fast but less accurate coarse simulation.
method_or_artifact: Multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization with cross-evaluation across simulators of different fidelity and calibration using high-fidelity data.
workload_or_benchmark: Microarchitecture parameter exploration for the open-source XiangShan high-performance processor core.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Open-source high-performance processor and multiple simulators with differing fidelity; parameter space, simulator identities, calibration model, and hardware targets are not reported.
metrics: exploration efficiency and evaluation accuracy (numeric results not reported in the description)
limits: The description does not report search budgets, objective functions, simulator errors, convergence, baseline results, or processor configurations; it establishes the method and application but not quantitative superiority.

title: Capbench: A Multi-PDK Dataset for Machine-Learning-Based Post-Layout Capacitance Extraction
evidence_span: CapBench provides a reproducible capacitance-extraction dataset from 14 OpenROAD runs across ASAP7, NanGate45, and Sky130HD, with 61,855 3D windows and RWCap labels validated against Raphael at 0.64% mean absolute error. Ten ML architectures are evaluated: CNNs achieve 1.75% error, while GNNs are up to 41.4x faster with 10.2% error.
problem: Post-layout capacitance extraction requires expensive high-fidelity solvers, while ML models need reproducible multi-technology data for transfer and scalability studies.
method_or_artifact: Multi-PDK, multi-representation dataset built from placed-and-routed open-source designs, with high-fidelity random-walk labels, industry-tool validation, and benchmark evaluations across CNN, point-cloud transformer, and GNN models.
workload_or_benchmark: Single-core CPUs, SoCs, and media accelerators; 14 OpenROAD runs across ASAP7, NanGate45, and Sky130HD; 61,855 3D windows in three size tiers.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Three named technology nodes and OpenROAD physical-design flows; RWCap and Raphael extraction conditions, window construction, and transfer splits require detailed dataset documentation.
baselines: CNN, point-cloud transformer, and GNN architectures
metrics: 0.64% total-capacitance MAE for RWCap versus Raphael validation
limits: The description does not expose train/test leakage controls, per-node error distributions, absolute runtimes, license details, or model implementation; the dataset supports reproducibility claims but not automatic transfer generalization.

title: ChatSVA: Bridging SVA Generation for Hardware Verification via Task-Specific LLMs
evidence_span: ChatSVA is an end-to-end SystemVerilog Assertion generation system built on a multi-agent AgentBridge platform for data generation, augmentation, validation, and modular verification subtasks. It reports 98.66% syntax pass rate, 96.12% function pass rate, an average of 139.5 SVAs per design, 82.50% function coverage, and a public web service.
problem: Manual SVA authoring is labor-intensive and error-prone despite functional verification consuming a large part of the IC development lifecycle.
method_or_artifact: Task-specific multi-agent LLM system that decomposes SVA generation into data, augmentation, validation, and verifiable subtasks; public web service artifact.
workload_or_benchmark: SystemVerilog assertion generation across hardware designs; exact design suite, property distribution, and reference-assertion construction are not stated.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Digital hardware verification using SVA and an LLM-based service; model identities, prompts, simulator, design languages beyond SVA, and execution cost are not reported.
limits: The description omits design-suite composition, oracle construction, duplicate/assertion quality checks, model and prompt details, latency/cost, and comparison baselines; pass rates do not by themselves establish formal proof completeness.
